notes_sections.title: Time Difference Problems (Advanced)
notes_sections.content:
When a person travels the same distance at two different speeds and the time difference is given, use:

Time difference = D(1/x − 1/y)

Shortcut formula for distance:
D = (Time Difference × x × y) / (y − x)

Example:
A person reaches 1 hour late at 60 km/h and on time at 80 km/h.
D = (1 × 60 × 80) / (80 − 60)
D = 4800 / 20 = 240 km.

notes_sections.title: Advanced Average Speed Cases
notes_sections.content:
Average Speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time.

If different speeds are used for different time intervals, calculate distance separately.

Example:
3 hours at 40 km/h and 2 hours at 60 km/h.
Total Distance = 120 + 120 = 240 km
Total Time = 5 hours
Average Speed = 48 km/h.

notes_sections.title: Boat and Stream
notes_sections.content:
Downstream Speed = Boat Speed + Stream Speed
Upstream Speed = Boat Speed − Stream Speed

Boat Speed = (Downstream + Upstream) / 2
Stream Speed = (Downstream − Upstream) / 2

Example:
Downstream = 20 km/h
Upstream = 12 km/h
Boat Speed = 16 km/h
Stream Speed = 4 km/h.

notes_sections.title: Advanced Train Crossing Problems
notes_sections.content:
When two trains cross each other:
Time = (Sum of lengths) ÷ Relative Speed

Opposite direction → Add speeds
Same direction → Subtract speeds

Example:
Train A = 120 m, Train B = 180 m
Speeds = 20 m/s and 30 m/s (opposite direction)
Time = (300) ÷ (50) = 6 seconds.

notes_sections.title: Speed Percentage Change Impact
notes_sections.content:
If speed increases by p%,
Time decreases by p / (100 + p) × 100%

If speed decreases by p%,
Time increases by p / (100 − p) × 100%

Example:
Speed increases by 25%
Time decreases by 25/125 × 100 = 20%.

notes_sections.title: Speed Ratio and Time Ratio (Distance Constant)
notes_sections.content:
If speed ratio = a : b
Then time ratio = b : a

Example:
Speed ratio = 4 : 5
Time ratio = 5 : 4.

notes_sections.title: Common Mistakes
notes_sections.content:
1. Forgetting to convert units before solving.
2. Taking simple average instead of weighted average.
3. Confusing upstream and downstream formulas.
4. Using addition instead of subtraction in same-direction problems.

notes_sections.title: Quick Summary
notes_sections.content:
Use proper formulas for time difference.
Average speed = Total Distance ÷ Total Time.
Relative speed depends on direction.
Boat and stream use half-sum and half-difference formulas.
Always check units.

tricks.title: Time Difference Direct Formula
tricks.explanation: Use D = (Time Difference × x × y) / (y − x) to directly find distance.
tricks.example: Speeds 50 & 75, time diff 2 hr → D = (2×50×75)/25 = 300 km.

tricks.title: Equal Distance Average Shortcut
tricks.explanation: If distances are equal, use (2xy)/(x+y) immediately.

tricks.title: Boat Speed Quick Trick
tricks.explanation: Add upstream and downstream speeds, divide by 2.

tricks.title: Stream Speed Quick Trick
tricks.explanation: Subtract upstream from downstream, divide by 2.

tricks.title: 18/5 Conversion Trick
tricks.explanation: Multiply by 18/5 to convert m/s to km/h instantly.

tricks.title: Ratio-Based Solving
tricks.explanation: Use inverse ratio when distance is constant to avoid full calculation.
